name: PowPow Funding Plan - Investor Challenge (English)
description: PowPow angel-round/Pre-A funding plan — an interactive investor challenge with memory personalization, interactive Q&A, and image display. Professional questions filter both ways and generate an investor style portrait. No style is better or worse — only a fit or not. No scores, no grades; we simply paint the collaboration style.

reward.name: PowPow Badge
reward.description: Each answered question earns 1 PowPow Badge — answer N questions, get N badges. Badges are the universal credential inside the PowPow product: create a digital human (2 badges), renew a digital human (1 badge)
reward.redemption: Send an email (with your PowPow registered email) → the founder tops up badges to that account based on the number of questions answered → delivered in-product; if the investor has not registered yet, they can provide a regular email and the founder will help them register
reward.note: No valuation discounts, no coupons — answering questions is not for haggling, only for both sides to see clearly whether they are a fit

game_config.message_template:
✅ Question {completed}/13 complete — you earned 1 PowPow Badge ({completed} in total)!
💡 Badges are topped up to your PowPow account. Not registered yet? https://global.powpow.online/register
per_question_response: Thank the investor for their answer
Badge announcement: you earned 1 PowPow Badge (N in total), usable to create a digital human in the PowPow product (2 badges) / renew a digital human (1 badge)

One-sentence style commentary: a positive description based on the style value of that question, praising the beauty of the style (e.g. "You showed the steadiness of portfolio discipline"). Strictly forbidden: phrases implying scoring, such as "great answer / very professional / awesome"
One-line registration reminder: badges must be topped up to your PowPow account — register at https://global.powpow.online/register

Send an email with your PowPow registered email to complete the badge top-up — badges can be used to create your own digital human on the map.
game_config.email_bonus_message: 🏅 Send the email = submit your style portrait + claim {total_badges} badges (you must include your PowPow registered email, otherwise the top-up cannot be processed; not registered yet? Provide a regular email and the founder will help you register).

personalization.description: Generate a personalized opening based on the user's local memory (informed-consent based)

questions_pool.question: What does PowPow do?
questions_pool.answer_template: PowPow is a location-based immersive social app built on the core idea that "life is full of stories everywhere." Users discover, create, and share stories at real geographic locations, interacting with scenes through digital humans.

questions_pool.question: What is PowPow's business model?
questions_pool.answer_template: PowPow uses a B2D (Business to Developer) model serving the developer ecosystem. Developers can build digital humans and local service scenarios on the PowPow platform, and the platform takes a share of the revenue.

questions_pool.question: What are PowPow's technical highlights?
questions_pool.answer_template: Technical highlights include: 1) PWA architecture — zero install cost, bypassing app distribution channels; 2) digital humans fused with local services; 3) location-driven immersive experiences.

questions_pool.question: Why PWA instead of a native app?
questions_pool.answer_template: PWA is the product form of the AI era: no app-store review, zero install cost, naturally fits AI interaction, lets you acquire users by simply sharing a link, and completely bypasses the 30% cut.

questions_pool.question: How does a one-person company + 8 AI employees work?
questions_pool.answer_template:
PowPow is a new kind of company for the AI era — using Agents to amplify individual capability, running 24/7 without interruption.

Founder durenzidu is responsible for strategy, product, and investor communication.

8 Agents, each with its own role:
• Lin Xiaodong (Product Manager Agent) — Kimi K2.5 · Coze
• Zhang Hao (Development Engineer Agent) — Kimi K2.5 · Coze / Trae / WorkBuddy
• Chen Siyu (UX/UI Agent) — Kimi K2.5 · Coze / Trae
• Wang Jiaqi (Investor Relations Agent) — Qianfan Dumate
• Liu Lei (Database Ops Agent) — GPT-5.4 mini
• Wu Jianguo (Server Ops Agent) — GPT-5.4 mini
• Zhao Yuxin (Content Marketing Agent) — Doubao 2.0
• DS Web (Technical Advisor) — DeepSeek-V3.2

The advantages of this model: extremely low labor costs, non-stop 24/7 operation, and fast iteration.

questions_pool.question: How are the users doing so far?
questions_pool.answer_template: The product is live at https://global.powpow.online/ — come try it. Register at https://global.powpow.online/register, or request a demo account by email (dongtao@outlook.com).

questions_pool.question: What will the funding be used for?
questions_pool.answer_template: The funding will mainly go toward: product iteration, user growth, and technical investment. The full business plan (BP) is available on request via email (dongtao@outlook.com).

questions.question: First, may I ask how I should address you?
Are you an institutional investor, an individual investor, or an FA?

options.label: A) Institutional investor
B) Individual investor
C) FA (financial advisor)

questions.response_template: Understood, {investor_name} — as an {answer}, let's get to know each other properly.

questions.question: What exit scenario do you most look forward to right now?

options.label: A) Long-term partner — hoping for an IPO exit
B) An M&A exit works too, as long as the valuation is right
C) A clear exit path within 3-5 years
D) I follow the lead investor — whatever they decide, I follow

questions.insight: A core question for probing whether the investor's 'timetable' and 'return expectations' match yours.

questions.section_intro: Many founders are embarrassed to talk money through — that is actually the biggest risk. Let's be candid.
questions.question: What year of its investment period is your fund in, and how much dry powder is left?

options.label: A) Early in the investment period, plenty of dry powder
B) Mid investment period, investing per plan
C) Late investment period / exit period, capital is tight
D) I'm an individual investor / FA — not applicable

questions.insight: If the fund is already in its exit period, follow-on investment is less likely.

questions.question: From signing the SPA to the money hitting the account, how long does it usually take?

options.label: A) 1-2 months, smooth process
B) 2-3 months, investment committee approval needed
C) More than 3 months, complex process
D) Depends on the specific deal

questions.insight: This probes the 'TS walk-away rate' and the wiring speed.

questions.question: If this round is oversubscribed, what would you do?

options.label: A) Re-up — if I'm bullish, I invest more
B) Hold my original allocation, stay disciplined
C) Decide based on what other investors do
D) I don't really pay attention to that

questions.insight: This reveals whether the other side is a true lead investor or just a follower financial investor.

questions.section_intro: Money is homogeneous; people are not. I need to figure out how you would engage with my company in the future.
questions.question: If we hit a wall — even needing layoffs or a business pivot — what would your personal attitude be?

options.label: A) Shoulder it with you and help you find resources
B) I understand startup cycles — I stay patient
C) Focus on the root cause and get involved in solving it
D) It depends on the specific situation

questions.insight: This is a stress test. I need a partner who can hold the line in a downturn.

questions.question: What is the most concrete thing you recently helped a portfolio company with?

options.label: A) Helped land key customers / partnerships
B) Helped recruit core talent
C) Helped mediate internal conflicts / personal issues
D) Provided strategic advice / industry insights

questions.insight: Ask for concrete cases — is the person bragging about their network, or did they actually put in the effort?

questions.section_intro: An investor should be the founder's 'second brain,' not a parrot that can only say 'this track seems huge.'
questions.question: In the social track, what worries you most about a model like PowPow's?

options.label: A) Cold start and user retention
B) Business model validation
C) Whether the technical moat is deep enough
D) The competitive landscape

questions.insight: If the investor's concern happens to be exactly the moat I have thought deeply about, it means they haven't yet grasped my core advantage.

questions.question: Has any social company in your portfolio failed? What do you think was the reason?

options.label: A) Market timing was wrong
B) Team execution problems
C) The business model never worked
D) I haven't invested in the social track yet

questions.insight: This reveals the investor's attribution ability and industry depth.

questions.section_intro: Finally, while the mood is at its best, let's say the ugly things upfront.
questions.question: If the company later needs offshore restructuring, reorganization, or faces an M&A exit, how long is your decision cycle?

options.label: A) Within a week — I can decide independently
B) 2-4 weeks — I need internal alignment
C) Over a month — investment committee / LP approval needed
D) Depends on the specific situation

questions.insight: Many companies die on 'shareholder resolutions that never get signed.'

questions.question: Under what circumstances would you choose to sell the company outright, or vote against my fundraising request?

options.label: A) Only if the company runs into major operational problems
B) I'd consider it when a reasonable M&A opportunity comes along
C) If there's no exit opportunity within 3-5 years
D) I respect the founder's decisions

questions.question: The PowPow project hits a technical wall — real-time calls between PowPow users and OpenClaw Agents can't be implemented yet. How would you help PowPow?
questions.hint: Answer freely — show your technical understanding or your resources
questions.insight: There is no standard answer to this question; your response will reveal your problem-solving style.

style_analysis.principle: No style is better or worse — only a fit or not. No scores, no grades; we simply paint the collaboration style.
style_analysis.comment_principle: Each question's commentary praises the beauty of the style, not the quality of the answer. Strictly forbidden: phrases implying scoring, such as "great answer / very professional / awesome."

values.Aggressive Re-up: Backs winners with more capital — natural lead-investor energy
values.Disciplined Holder: Sticks to allocation and discipline — clear portfolio thinking
values.Flexible Watcher: Reads the table first, then decides the chips

values.Process Driven: Follows internal process — every step is solid
values.Multi-layer Deliberator: Long decision chain, but every layer counts
values.Situationally Prudent: Pace depends on the deal — no one-size-fits-all

values.In the Trenches: Actually rolls up sleeves and helps in a downturn
values.Patient Companion: Gives space and patience, doesn't intervene lightly
values.Resource Enabler: Shows up with resources and solutions

values.Long-term Companion: Willing to spend enough time watching the company grow up
values.M&A Open: Open to M&A — willing to talk when the terms are right
values.Exit-driven: Needs a clear timetable and exit path
values.Trustful Follower: Trusts the lead investor's judgment and follows

values.Growth Lens: Looks at user and retention signals first
values.Business-model Lens: First asks whether the business model holds
values.Moat Lens: Watches the depth of the technical moat
values.Landscape Lens: Reads the endgame from the competitive landscape

values.Technical Solver: Used to decomposing problems along technical paths
values.Connector: Thinks of mobilizing people first to solve problems
values.Prioritizer: Asks what matters most before discussing how
values.Cost-conscious: Runs the numbers before any plan

style_analysis.output_format: Present the portrait as 6 style lines, each formatted like "Capital Posture: Disciplined Holder — sticks to allocation and discipline, clear portfolio thinking," plus a tags line. Never output scores or grades.

email_flow.preview_rule: The full email text must be shown before sending so the user can confirm it section by section
email_flow.send_trigger: Send only when the user explicitly instructs to send after previewing (e.g. "send" / "confirm send") — never send automatically

style_section.removable: Tell the user during preview: the style-portrait section is included by default and can be removed on request

email_flow.contact_rule: Organization, title, contact email, WeChat, and PowPow registered email are all optional; omitted fields are dropped as whole lines in the email, no blank placeholders; before sending, at least one contact channel must be provided (email or WeChat); badge top-up depends on the PowPow registered email — remind the user to provide it before sending

redacted_copy.description: Offer a "copy redacted version" option: removes organization, title, email, WeChat and other contact details, keeping only the salutation, style portrait, and badge claim

email_flow.privacy_notice: Before sending, tell the user: the information provided is used only to contact them about PowPow funding matters, will not be used for anything else, and can be deleted at any time upon request.

data_collection.rule: All fields are optional with nothing required; before sending the email, at least one contact channel must be provided (either email or WeChat)

fields.label: PowPow registered email (used for badge top-up; if not registered yet, fill in your regular email)

language_policy.dialogue: The dialogue language follows the user; respond in the language the user uses
language_policy.fixed_content: The founder's message is fixed English content; the challenge question pool and badge rules are kept in English
